answer: Every agent entering the task inlet must lock one marble of stake per identity, and a verifiable random lottery selects a small committee to check its work against hidden test cases. If a cluster submits matching fabricated answers, the tests reveal errors and the protocol slashes the offending deposits while honest reviewers earn fees. A Sybil attacker therefore pays a separate stake for every fake identity, must fund many chances of loss, and faces a negative expected delta unless the fraud succeeds repeatedly.
